newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher, with many indexes rallying late on Greenspan-related relief.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to a House Banking subcommittee this afternoon ended with no statements admonishing the high level of U.S. stocks, like those heard last week and in December.
"I think it was what he failed to say this time that drove us higher," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
The firm tone began earlier on Wednesday with comments from Greenspan at a business economists' breakfast.
Greenspan said the stock market was properly priced if Wall Street estimates for corporate profit growth proved correct.

March Standard and Poor's 500 futures rallied above resistance at 797.00 and 798.10 early to finally push into key 800.00 territory in afternoon trading. Traders noted aggressive buy stops at 800.00 and above 802.00 and said both are now support levels for Thursday.
"Tomorrow morning you have to keep an eye on 802.00 for any pullback," one trader said. "If they fail through there, 800.00 is most likely going to trade very quickly," he said.
But overall, "the market looks powerful again," he said.

Others worried about jitters Thursday as February non-farm payrolls data loom. A Reuters poll of economists pegged an average estimate of 230,000 jobs added in February. Worries of strong economic growth as reflected in a hefty jobs number could restrain bond prices again, traders said.
"We could be spinning our wheels until we see what jobs say about the economy," the trader said.
Traders said dealers were good March S&P 500 buyers in the afternoon, with a Chicago bank a seller on the day of 800 contracts.
U.S. January housing completions were reported down 9.9 percent to a 1.324 million annual rate.

At the close, March S&Ps were up 12.20 points at 804.25, KCBT Value Lines rose 6.40 to 716.20, Nikkeis were 190.0 lower at 18,445.0, Midcap rose 1.40 to 265.40, NYSE Composite rose 6.10 to 422.00, and Nasdaq 100s were up 12.50 at 875.75.
